page: Microsoft Azure E64-16as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EASv4 family. It is equipped with 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The underlying virtualization is managed by Microsoft Hyper-V. A key hardware highlight is the substantial memory allocation of 512.0 GB, which translates to 32.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided via an 885 GB SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core results placing in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU benchmarks, including Geekbench and PassMark CPU tests, fall into the average tier. Memory performance is mixed; while the PassMark memory score is strong, the large-block uncached memory write bandwidth is weak, measuring at 22.75 GB/sec. Other operations, such as Redis SET and static web serving, maintain average throughput levels.

This hardware profile offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound applications that require high memory density relative to compute resources. It is highly suitable for large in-memory databases, caching systems, and enterprise applications that demand extensive memory capacity without requiring massive parallel CPU scaling.
